items.title: Polanski failed to show leadership over Zionism motion, ex-Green leader says
items.summary: Caroline Lucas tells the BBC Zack Polanski should have taken part in a vote on a motion declaring Zionism a form of racism.

items.title: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review
items.summary: The review, which focuses on younger people, warned there was a risk society was moving from an era of under-diagnosis to over-diagnosis.

items.title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says
items.summary: A criminal investigation into the former prince continues and police have retained material seized from his homes.

items.title: Suspect linked to Monaco bomb attack on millionaire breaks silence to BBC
items.summary: Vitalii Zhykovych gives his own account of the attempted assassination of Ukrainian-born businessman Vadym Yermolayev.

items.title: Fort Hood attacker's execution by firing squad will be livestreamed, Pentagon says
items.summary: The US Defence Secretary says the execution will be public, but a legal expert says the "unprecedented" decision is on "uncertain legal terrain".

items.title: Emotions run high at the round table as Celebrity Traitors banish two players
items.summary: Viewers watched to see whether Richard E Grant could save himself at the first round table of the series.

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg has an image problem - so why is Meta's business booming?
items.summary: A new film paints the Meta founder as a villain. But the tech firm seems immune to bad publicity, writes our North America tech correspondent.

items.title: 'Add me to WhatsApp' scam calls to be investigated
items.summary: The UK's data watchdog is investigating a spike in complaints about "robo calls" that appear to lead to a recruitment scam.
